heard: An octopus has three beating hearts and bright blue-copper-based blood. Stepping up in scale from single-heart creatures, this soft-bodied marine genius lacks bones entirely to squeeze through tiny gaps. Climbing higher along the biological scale, the entire animal possesses around 500 million total neural connections. Reaching the absolute peak of the scale, two-thirds of those massive neurological counts live directly inside its eight arms. Each arm operates with semi-independence, tasting and touching without waiting for commands from the central brain. Some clever individuals even collect discarded coconut shells for portable shelter across the ocean floor. An octopus has three beating hearts and bright blue copper-based blood.
